significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that across several jailbreak classes, "the per-position harm signal at the harm-bearing tokens remains largely intact, but its projection into the final decision position collapses," and that disrupted routing causally drives compliance; this is a form-(iii) positional coupling plus a form-(ii) decomposition of representation failure from read-out failure. It establishes both a cross-attack phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing the expectation that attacks preserving local harm evidence should remain detectable by position aggregation and should respond to restored routing; this matters mechanistically because Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction" (NeurIPS 2024), makes low-dimensional refusal geometry a concrete basis for safety interventions. The claim is determinate despite qualifiers such as "largely": a negative result showing harm signals disappear throughout the prompt, or do not predict final-position collapse, would reject the proposed unifying account and support representation-defeating rather than read-out-defeating explanations. Topic-substitution check: replacing this representation-versus-routing decomposition with the generic goal of mechanistic LLM safety would not justify the score; the extra weight comes from the specific conserved-local-signal/failing-final-read-out relation across distinct attacks.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "distributed-aggregation monitor" that pools latent harm evidence "across all prompt positions"; it is ex ante because it can flag a harmful input before the model produces the refusal-or-compliance outcome, giving deployers an opportunity to gate generation. After per-model probe re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—preserved evidence at harm-bearing positions alongside collapsed final-position evidence—rather than merely prescribing an open-ended search, although its numeric thresholds and directions would still require calibration. The asserted scope covers Llama, Qwen, and Gemma families, multiple jailbreak types, and held-out attacks, so downstream users include safety auditors and deployment practitioners, but the explicit statement that "frontier transfer is untested" and the need for activation access keep it below universal or outside-AI reach. Topic-substitution check: generic interpretability for safer LLMs would not supply this pre-generation monitor or its positional prediction, so the score rests on claim-specific lead time and practitioner uptake rather than on the safety topic itself.
